question: What is the radius (in cm) of a circle whose areas is {2(17)/(30)} times the sum of the areas of two triangles whose sides are 20 cm, 21 cm and 29 cm, and 11 cm, 60 cm and 61 cm (take π = {(22)/(7)})?
solution:
**Given**

Area of circle = {2(17)/(30)}(sum of the area of two triangles)

**Concept**

if the sum of the squares of the two sides of a triangle is equal to the square of hypotenuse side, then triangle is right angled triangle.

(H)² = (P)² + (B)²

**Calculation**

(20)² + (21)² = (29)²

400 + 441 = 841

841 = 841

Area of triangle = (1/2) × base × height

⇒ (1/2) × 20 × 21

⇒ 210 cm²

(11)² + (60)² = (61)²

121 + 3600 = 3721

3721 = 3721

Area of triangle = (1/2) × 60 × 11

⇒ 330 cm²

Area of circle = 77/30 × (210 + 330)

⇒ (77/30) × 540

⇒ 1386 cm²

(22/7) × r² = 1386

r² = 1386 × (7/22)

r² = 9702/22

r² = 441

r = 2**1**

**∴ Radius of circle is 21 cm**
